description: A dentist has 3000 units of resin to fill cavities in both molars and canines. Molars require 20 units of resin and 3 units of pain killer. Canines require 15 units of resin and 2.3 units of pain killer. Since this dentist sees more cavities in canines, at least 60% of cavities filled must be in canines. In addition, the dentist must reserve materials to fill at least 45 molars. How many of each type of teeth should the dentist schedule to fill to minimize the amount of pain killer needed?

TotalResin.definition: Total amount of resin available for filling cavities

ResinPerMolar.definition: Units of resin required to fill one molar

ResinPerCanine.definition: Units of resin required to fill one canine

PainKillerPerMolar.definition: Units of pain killer required to fill one molar

PainKillerPerCanine.definition: Units of pain killer required to fill one canine

MinPercentageCanines.definition: Minimum fraction of cavities filled that must be canines

MinNumMolars.definition: Minimum number of molars that must be filled

objective.description: "Minimize the total amount of pain killer required to fill the scheduled molars and canines"

constraints.description: Total resin used for molars and canines should not exceed the total resin available: ResinPerMolar * M + ResinPerCanine * C ≤ TotalResin
At least 60% of the total cavities filled must be canines: C ≥ MinPercentageCanines * (M + C)
At least the minimum required number of molars must be filled: M ≥ MinNumMolars
